usageNotes: Use this to grant or revoke a role on an ACL path for a specific auth-id (user or API token) or group — supply exactly one of `auth-id` or `group`, not both. Set `delete: true` to remove the permission instead of adding it. Use the `digest` parameter when making changes in scripts to guard against concurrent modifications overwriting each other.

examples.summary: Grant the Administrator role to a user at the root path with propagation enabled

tips: Only one of `auth-id` or `group` should be provided per call; supplying neither results in an error.
The `path` must match the ACL path hierarchy used by PDM (e.g., `/`, `/mapping`, `/remotes/my-remote`); invalid paths are rejected.
Tokens (auth-id with `!` separator, e.g., `admin@pam!mytoken`) can only be granted roles that are a subset of the owning user's roles — PDM enforces this automatically.
Returns null on success; no confirmation body is returned, so verify with get_access_acl after making changes.
Setting `propagate: false` scopes the permission strictly to that path and does not cascade to child paths.
